name: Paper
tagline: Browser-based design tool for vector layouts and motion, aimed at designers who want interactive, animated output instead of static frames.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: This is a real-time graphics engine wearing a design tool costume. The hard parts are the parts nobody sees: a vector renderer that stays at 60fps with hundreds of nodes, boolean ops and path math that do not produce garbage, a constraint and layout system, an animation timeline with interpolation that matches what the browser will actually do, and multiplayer editing on top of all of it. An agent can absolutely give you a canvas where you drag rectangles and scrub keyframes, and that is fun for an afternoon. It falls apart the moment you want to do real work in it, because real work means precision, undo that never lies, and export that renders identically outside the editor. Tools like this are measured in engineer-years, not sessions.
coreLoopDIY: A local single-user canvas editor with shapes, a pen tool, layer tree, and a keyframe timeline that exports animated SVG plus a JSON scene file.
requirements: No accounts, no cloud, everything in localStorage and files on disk
Willingness to accept a toy renderer instead of a real one
whatYouLose: Renderer performance: your build will chug somewhere between 200 and 2000 nodes, theirs will not
Path math that actually works: booleans, offsets, strokes as outlines, corner radii on arbitrary paths
Multiplayer editing, comments, shared files, version history
Export fidelity, where the animation you previewed matches what ships
The thousand small correctness behaviors: snapping, nudge, alignment, undo grouping, clipboard, nested groups, constraints
moatNotes: Design tools are almost pure execution polish. There is no data moat and barely a network one, but the surface area of getting a canvas to feel right is enormous and unglamorous.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because feel is the product. A design tool that stutters, snaps wrong, or loses an undo step is not a cheaper version of a good design tool, it is unusable, and people notice within ten minutes. Everything worth paying for here is the accumulated correctness of a rendering and interaction layer that took a team years to sand down, plus the fact that your collaborators can open the same file. Nobody buys this because of a feature list; they buy it because dragging a handle does exactly what their hands expected.
notes: You can build a canvas with keyframes in a sitting; you cannot build a design tool. The moat is execution polish: thousands of small interaction and path-math correctness details plus a renderer that stays smooth, none of which show up in a feature comparison.
prompt:
Build a local, single-user vector animation editor that runs entirely in the browser. No accounts, no backend, no telemetry.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Vite + TypeScript + React for UI chrome only
- A single HTML canvas element for the scene, rendered with the 2D context, no SVG DOM for the editing surface
- Zustand for editor state, immer for immutable edits
- No design-tool libraries: write the scene graph, hit testing and transforms yourself

Scope that is IN:
- Scene graph: groups, rectangles, ellipses, polylines, text, each with x, y, w, h, rotation, fill, stroke, opacity, corner radius
- Tools: select, move, rectangle, ellipse, pen (click to add points, closes on first point), text
- Selection: click, shift-click multi-select, marquee drag, 8 resize handles plus rotate handle
- Snapping to other objects' edges and centers with pink guide lines, hold alt to disable
- Layer panel with drag reorder, rename, hide, lock, nested groups
- Properties panel bound to the current selection, multi-select edits apply to all
- Undo/redo with grouped transactions, so one drag is one undo step. This is non-negotiable, do it before adding features
- Timeline: 0 to 10 seconds, per-property keyframes on x, y, rotation, opacity, fill, linear plus ease-in-out interpolation, scrub head, spacebar to play
- Save/load the whole document as a .json file via file input and download
- Export: static SVG of the current frame, and an animated SVG using SMIL for keyframed properties

Scope that is OUT, do not attempt:
- Multiplayer, comments, cloud sync, sharing links
- Boolean path operations, path offsetting, stroke-to-outline
- Auto layout, constraints, components or instances
- Plugins, code export beyond SVG, image import

Requirements:
- Keyboard: v/r/o/p/t for tools, delete, cmd+z, cmd+shift+z, cmd+g group, cmd+d duplicate, arrow nudge
- Autosave the document to localStorage on every committed transaction, restore on load
- Redraw only on state change, keep the render loop off when idle and during playback only
- Ship a README that states plainly what is missing and where it will get slow
- Any secrets, if you ever add any, go in .env and never in the repo
